content:
**brain:check issueLink needs a real closing keyword, "Part of #N" only works off-main**

What: npm run brain:check's issueLink policy check (brain/scripts/brain-check.mjs, backed by brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.mjs via the shared evaluator, #340) reads the LATEST COMMIT'S BODY and requires a real closing keyword — Close(s|d)|Fix(es|ed)|Resolve(s|d) #N — when the target branch resolves to the repo default (main), which it does whenever no PR exists yet (#340's ruling: default to the stricter default-branch rule rather than assume the laxer slice rule). "Part of #N" alone is accepted only when targeting a non-default (slice) branch.

Why: hit this while committing docs for issue #755 in a worktree — first tried "Part of #755" in the commit body and brain:check FAILed issueLink with an explicit message naming the accepted forms. Amended the final commit's body to "Closes #755" and it passed (locally the same run then surfaced a separate UNVERIFIED for issueLink — `gh api repos/undefined/issues/755` 404s — because the worktree's gh remote/repo resolution didn't produce an owner/repo; that part is an environment limitation of the standalone worktree, not a content defect).

Where: brain/scripts/brain-check.mjs; brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.mjs (the pure check + policy).

Learned: amending the tip commit (not adding a third commit) was the right move here to keep the "exactly two commits" contract intact for a two-work-unit change — brain:check only looks at the LATEST commit's body, not any commit in the branch.
